nar.text: Because the dirt road circuit was rather narrow at some places and difficult for drivers to pass each other, as a safety precaution the cars were started individually from a standing start
The actual start began at 3:00 PM on the Boulevard Prince of Naples, when Princess Maria Ciano gave the signal to the drivers and Moradei's Salmson with the lowest number 2 was released.
Moradei's Salmson is first past the grandstands, finishing the first lap in 18m36s; Ernesto Maserati has already passed Villa and Sartorio on the road.
During the second lap Brilli Peri still held the lead with a lap of 15m27.2s a new record at an average speed of 87.358 km/h, ahead of Varzi, Nuvolari and Pastore.
Villa retired the Derby with mechanical failure.
Decaroli stopped his Bugatti at the pits which dropped him seven places.
During the third lap Brilli Peri maintained his lead and held an advantage of 12 seconds to Varzi.
Moradei stopped at his pit with a steering problem. Ruggeri, Giorgini and Sartorio also made pit stops.
After four laps Brilli Peri still prevailed just three seconds ahead of Varzi, followed by Nuvolari, Biondetti now in fourth place and Pastore.
Ernesto Maserati made a brief pit stop. Giorgini retired the O.M with mechanical failure.
Varzi laps in a record 15m11.8s and takes the lead; Brilli Peri is 14 seconds behind.
Campari, who inherited fifth place when Pastore stopped at his pit.
Varzi lowers the lap record to 15m10.4s and leads Brilli Peri by 39 seconds.
Pastore in tenth place stopped again at his pit.
Brilli Peri was pressured by Nuvolari, who was now only 16 seconds behind.
Morandi was forced to retire on lap seven when a lever of the gearbox broke and Ruggeri also called it quits on that lap.
On lap eight Varzi carried on in first place when Brilli Peri stopped at his pit and lost two positions.
Nuvolari inherited second place almost two minutes behind and Biondetti was now third.
Sartorio retired his Amilcar with mechanical failure on this lap when the field was down to 17 cars after eight laps.

After the ninth lap Varzi was still out front ahead of Nuvolari and Campari, who had moved into third place. Arcangeli had passed into fourth spot followed by Biondetti, who had a problem with his car and Brilli Peri, who was once more delayed with another pit stop.
Varzi wins in a record 2h34m51.5s.
Nuvolari followed two and a half minutes behind with a lap of 15m43.6s, while Campari finished third driving his fastest lap at the end in 15m29.6s ahead of Arcangeli's 1500 Talbot.
Biondetti, who began the last lap in fifth place, encountered engine problems on the last lap and retired.
Brilli Peri drove his last lap in exactly 16 minutes, finishing a disappointing fifth.
In the 1100 class Bucci ran into trouble and lost his lead which gave the class victory to Moradei.
